item.title: Recipes: Make these dishes for a delicious and healthy Ramadan

item.title: Phillies’ Bryce Harper still chafes at Dave Dombrowski’s ‘elite’ questioning
item.description: Phillies first baseman Bryce Harper said Sunday “it's kind of wild to me still” that president of baseball operations Dave Dombrowski suggested in October the two-time NL MVP may no longer be an elite player.

item.title: DNA recovered from glove found near Guthrie home that appears to match glove worn by suspect, FBI says
item.description: The FBI says a glove containing DNA was found about two miles from Nancy Guthrie's house and appears to match those worn by a masked person seen outside her front door.

item.title: HS BASKETBALL: Matchups set for opening round of district playoffs
item.description: The pairings for the District 2 basketball tournaments, which get underway Tuesday night, were officially released by the District 2 Committee. On Tuesday, the Class 4A and 5A boys brackets get under way, and the girls Class 2A, 3A and 6A tournaments begin. In boys Class 4A, Dallas is the top seed and will host Mid Valley. Hanover Area plays at Valley View, Tunkhannock plays at Wyoming Area and Honesdale is at Scranton Prep. All games begin at 7 p.m. In boys Class 5A, North Pocono is at Wallenpa

item.title: Police: Shickshinny woman removed security devices from apparel at Dick’s
item.description: The jailed 42-year-old woman is charged with removing security devices from $658 worth of merchandise at the Scranton store on Wednesday.

item.title: COUNTERPOINT: Enforcing immigration law benefits Americans
item.description: The administration is right to argue that enforcing immigration laws gets criminal aliens out of communities.

item.title: POINT: Legal immigration boosts America’s innovation advantage
item.description: America’s economic strength rests on its ability to attract talent, reward hard work, and out-innovate global competitors.

item.title: : EditorialWe must protect Pennsylvania’s young people from chatbots
item.description: During Gov. Josh Shapiro’s lengthy and, on occasion, unusually partisan budget address this past Tuesday, one theme attracted significant support from both parties: preserving children and childhood from predatory technologies.

item.title: Jr. HIGH BASKETBALL: Anthracite League playoffs scheduled
item.description: The Anthracite Junior High Basketball League’s postseason tournament will gets under way with girls and boys’ doubleheaders at Hazleton Area High School’s Hughie McGeehan Gymnasium. Tuesday, the girls will take center stage with Hazleton taking on McAdoo-Kelayres at 6 p.m. followed by West Hazleton meeting Valley at 7. In boys’ semifinal action on Thursday, West Hazleton will face Heights-Terrace at 6 and Valley and Drums will clash at 7. Semifinal winners in both the boys and girls’ tournaments

item.title: COMMUNITY DIGEST: Feb. 16, 2026
item.description: Greater Hazleton Area and beyond Hazleton Art League’s Annual Member Show: Through Feb. 22. Hayden Family Center for the Arts, 31 W. Broad St., Hazleton. The Members’ Exhibition is one of the Art League’s most popular events of the year, showcasing the talent of local artists. Many of the featured works will be available for purchase, with a portion of each sale supporting the Hazleton Art League. For information, call 570-455-3333 or visit hazletonartleague.org.
